ingredients.name: Yellowfin tuna (kelawalla)
ingredients.notes: cut into 5cm cubes; fresh or thawed from frozen; firm flesh holds up well in curry

ingredients.name: Red chilli powder
ingredients.notes: for the marinade; use Kashmiri for a milder heat and deep red colour

ingredients.name: Roasted Sri Lankan curry powder
ingredients.notes: see sl_006; mixed into the marinade

ingredients.name: Lime
ingredients.notes: juiced; for the marinade -- firms the flesh and removes raw smell

ingredients.name: Tomato
ingredients.notes: chopped; adds body and slight sourness

ingredients.name: Goraka
ingredients.notes: small piece soaked in warm water; or substitute 1 tbsp tamarind paste

ingredients.name: Thick coconut milk
ingredients.notes: added at the very end; do not boil hard

steps.instruction: Mix the tuna cubes with turmeric, chilli powder, black pepper, roasted curry powder, lime juice, and salt. Set aside to marinate for 10-15 minutes.
Heat coconut oil in a wide shallow pan over medium heat. Add mustard seeds and let them crackle. Add fenugreek, cinnamon stick, curry leaves, and pandan leaf. Sizzle for 30 seconds.
Add sliced onion and cook until softened, about 4-5 minutes. Add garlic, ginger, and green chillies. Cook for another minute until fragrant.
Add the chopped tomatoes and goraka (or tamarind). Cook for 3-4 minutes until the tomatoes soften into the base.
Pour in the thin coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer. Add salt to taste.

Carefully add the marinated tuna pieces. Spoon some sauce over the top. Simmer gently without stirring for 8-10 minutes -- handle the fish as little as possible to avoid breaking up the pieces. Turn once gently halfway through if needed.

Once the tuna is cooked through, pour in the thick coconut milk. Gently shake the pan rather than stirring to distribute it. Simmer on the lowest heat for 2-3 minutes. Taste and adjust salt. Serve hot with rice, pittu, or string hoppers.

source_site: joyofeatingtheworld.com, cross-checked against propermasala.com, fragrantcurryleaves.com, islandsmile.org, loveandotherspices.com, chilliandmint.com, and disnies.lk
collection_method: scraped, cross-checked across 8+ independent sources; strong agreement on marinating, gentle handling to preserve fish shape, and thin-then-thick coconut milk technique
notes: Kelawalla (yellowfin tuna) is one of Sri Lanka's most abundant and beloved fish, and this coconut-milk curry (kirata/mirisata) is the most common everyday preparation distinct from the dry goraka-based ambul thiyal (sl_014). Unlike ambul thiyal which uses no coconut milk and is essentially a preservation technique, kelawalla malu kirata is a creamy, lightly spiced gravy curry eaten fresh. The key technique is gentle handling -- tuna breaks apart easily once cooked, so stirring should be minimised and the pan should be shaken rather than stirred once the fish is in. Propermasala.com highlights that the fish matters more than the spices in this dish -- the quality and freshness of the tuna drives most of the flavour.
